No. 113 of 2000, whereby the learned Tribunal had partly allowed the Claim Petition and awarded a sum of Rs.66,220/- (Sixty Six Thousand Two Hundred Twenty Only)

2. The succinct facts, which led to the filing of the captioned appeal, as explained by the learned counsel for the appellant and as narrated in NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2597/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/04/2026 undefined the Claim Petition are summarized as under:-
i.
On 13.07.1999 at about 3:30 p.m., the original claimant/appellant herein was riding a Motorcycle bearing registration No.GJ-1-AF-312 at very moderate speed from Naroda Bethak to Naroda Village.

When he reached near Anil Showroom, one Maruti car bearing registration No.GJ-1-RR-8688 being driven by original opponent No.1/
respondent No.1 herein at very excessive speed and in a rash and negligent manner,
came from the backside and dashed with the motorcycle on which the original claimant/appellant herein was travelling, thereby causing the vehicular accident.
As a result of the said vehicular accident, the original claimant/appellant herein sustained grievous injuries to his body.

ii. It is the case of the original claimant/appellant herein before the learned Tribunal that at the time of the vehicular accident, he was aged about 40 years and was earning Rs.8000/- per month, by working in Reliance Textiles and Tulsi Traders.

It is also the case of the original claimant/appellant herein that due to the injuries sustained in the vehicular accident, he had to undergo treatment for a considerable period of time and had suffered severe pain, shock & sufferings.
Therefore, the Original Claimant/appellant preferred the Claim Petition before the learned Tribunal seeking compensation to the tune of Rs.5,00,000/-.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2597/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/04/2026 undefined iii.

Having been served with the notices/summons of the Claim Petition,
the original opponent No.3/respondent No.3 herein - Insurer of the Maruti Car, filed its Written Statement at Exh.21, thereby denying the averments made in the Claim Petition, and in brief, prayed for dismissal of the Claim Petition.

iv. Having considered the pleadings of the parties and the material available on record, the learned Tribunal framed the following issues, for determination:-
i.

Whether the petitioner proves that he/she sustained grievous injuries in a vehicular accident by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle driven by its driver ?
ii. What amount of compensation the petitioner is entitled to and from whom ?
iii. What order and award ?

v. Having considered the pleadings, evidence on record and the submissions advanced by the learned counsels for the respective parties, the learned Tribunal partly allowed the Claim Petition and awarded a sum of Rs.66,220/- (Sixty Six Pradipbhai Tulsidas Doshi vs Lalabhai Gulabji Borina on 7 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77888595/
2 Thousand Two Hundred Twenty Only) along with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum, from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization, as compensation.

Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award, the original claimant/appellant herein has challenged the impugned judgment and award on the ground of meagreness of compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal.

3. Heard learned counsels for the parties.
4.

Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the original claimant/appellant herein vehemently submitted that at the time of the vehicular accident, the claimant/appellant herein was aged about 40 years and was working at Reliance Textiles, thereby earning Rs.6,324/- per month as salary,
however, the learned Tribunal had assessed the income of the claimant/appellant herein at very lower side.
He further submitted that in order to prove his income, the claimant/appellant herein has examined one Mr. Paresh S Nayak, who is an officer of Reliance Textiles at Exh. 44.

He further submitted that the Income Certificate of the claimant/appellant herein was proved at Exh.45,
however, despite this fact, the learned Tribunal, deducted amounts on account of HRA, Cola,
Conveyance allowance, Medical bills, LTA, Bonus from the gross salary of the claimant/appellant herein, and considered the income of the claimant/appellant herein at Rs.3.100/- per month.

He further submitted that the learned ought not to have deducted the said amounts on account of HRA,
Cola, Conveyance allowance, Medical bills, LTA, Bonus etc., from the gross salary of the claimant/appellant herein, in view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Vimal Kanwar and Others vs. Kishore Dan and Ors.

entities.text: Vimal Kanwar and Others vs. Kishore Dan and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: reported in (2013) 7 SCC 476.

Having placed reliance upon the aforesaid judgment, he contended that the learned Tribunal had committed manifest error in deducting amounts from the gross salary of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2597/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/04/2026 undefined the claimant/appellant herein.

5. Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the original claimant/appellant herein further submitted that the learned Tribunal had not considered the Future prospects of the claimant/appellant herein,
though at the time of the vehicular accident, the claimant/appellant herein was aged about 40 years,
therefore, the learned Tribunal ought to have added 25% of the notional monthly income to the monthly income of the claimant on account of his future prospects.
He further submitted that the learned Tribunal has wrongly applied the multiplier of "5" instead of "15.

In support of his contention, learned Counsel for the original claimant/appellant herein placed reliance upon the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Pranay Sethi reported in 2017 (16) SCC 680.

sentences.text: He contended that the learned Tribunal had awarded meagre amounts of compensation under the heads of Pain, shock & suffering, Medical expenses, Actual loss of income, Special Diet, Attendant & Transportation charges.

Therefore, he prayed for enhancement of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2597/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/04/2026 undefined compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal under the aforesaid heads and prayed for modification of the impugned judgment and award.

6. On the other hand, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent Nos. 2.1 & 2.2,
vehemently submitted that there is no infirmity in the impugned judgment and award.
He contended that the offending Maruti car was duly insured with respondent No.3 - Insurance Company, as such, no liability can be fastened upon respondent Nos. 2.1 & 2.2 herein.
He further contended that the captioned appeal is devoid of any merits and the same is liable to be dismissed.

7. Though Rule has been duly served upon the respondent No.3 - Insurance Company and Mr.
Nagesh C Sood has put his appearance on record, none appeared on behalf of the respondent No.3 - Insurance Company when the matter was called out in the morning session.

In order to facilitate the respondent No.3 - Insurance Company to advance arguments on its behalf, the matter was passed over and was taken up for hearing after the lunch session, however, despite this fact, nobody has bothered to appear on behalf of the respondent No.3 - Insurance Company.

8. Having considered the submissions of the learned counsels for the parties and having perused the material available on record, it is to be noted that the original claimant/appellant herein has challenged the impugned judgment and award on the ground of quantum.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2597/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/04/2026 undefined 9.

So far as the quantum awarded by the learned Tribunal is concerned, it is an undisputed fact that at the time of the vehicular accident, the claimant/appellant herein was working in Reliance Textiles.
The claimant/appellant herein had examined an officer of Reliance Textiles - Mr. Paresh S Nayak, at Exh.44.
He deposed that the claimant/appellant herein was working at Reliance Textiles.
He also proved the salary certificate of the claimant/appellant on record.
Perusal of the salary slip of the claimant/appellant herein proved at Exh.45 transpires that the gross salary of the claimant/appellant herein was Rs.6,324/- per month.

The learned Tribunal while considering the gross salary of the claimant/appellant herein, deducted amounts on account of HRA, Cola,
Conveyance allowance, Medical bills, LTA, Bonus etc., and considered the monthly income of the claimant/appellant herein as Rs.3,100/- per month.

In my considered view, the learned Tribunal ought not to have deducted the amount received by the claimant on account of HRA, Cola,
Conveyance allowance, Medical bills, LTA, Bonus etc., from the gross salary of the claimant/appellant herein, in view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Vimal Kanwar and Others (supra), wherein at Para No.21, the Hon'ble Apex Court had observed as under :-

sentences.text: "The third issue was "whether the income tax is liable to be deducted for determination of compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act".

The Supreme Court observed that in the case of Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation (2009) 6 SCC 121, it was held that "generally the actual income of the deceased less income tax should be the starting point for calculating the compensation".

It was further observed that NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2597/2014 JUDGMENT DATED:
07/04/2026 undefined "where the annual income is in taxable ran ge, the words "actual salary" should be read as "actual salary less tax".

10. Thus, having considered the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Vimal Kanwar and Others (supra), the income of the claimant/appellant herein is reassessed at Rs.6,324/-
per month.

11. It is not in dispute that at the time of the vehicular accident, the original claimant/appellant herein was aged about 40 years, as reflected from the cause title of the Claim Petition therefore, the notional monthly income of the original claimant/appellant herein is to be enhanced by 25% on account of the Future prospects of the original claimant/appellant herein.

Therefore, after adding 25% of the notional income to the monthly income of the original claimant/appellant herein, the monthly income of the original claimant/appellant herein would come to Rs.7,905/- (i.e, Rs.6,324/-
plus 25% of Rs.6,324/-).
12.
From the medical evidence available on record, it emerges that the claimant/appellant herein has sustained the permanent partial disability of 26% body as a whole.

The learned Tribunal without any reason or rhyme had reduced the said disability to 22%, though it is evident from the records that the claimant/appellant herein has sustained fractures to his right clavicle, 4th rib and 5th metacarpal on left hand.
Thus, having regard to the nature of work and the disability sustained by the claimant/appellant herein, the functional disability of the original claimant/appellant herein is taken at 26%.

13. The learned Tribunal had applied the multiplier of "5", though at the time of the vehicular accident, the claimant/appellant herein was NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2597/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/04/2026 undefined aged about 40 years.

Now it is well settled proposition in view of the ratio of the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra),
that multiplier has to applied as per the age of the claimant.
Thus, having regard to the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), multiplier of "15" is required to be applied.

Thus, after applying the multiplier of "15" as per age of the claimant/appellant herein,
the original claimant/appellant herein shall be entitled for a sum of Rs.3,69,954/- (i.e, Rs.7,905/- X 26% Disability X 12 months X multiplier of "15") under the head of Future Loss of income.
14. The learned Tribunal had awarded a sum of Rs.9,300/- under the head of Actual loss of income for a period of three months.
Now the monthly income of the claimant/appellant herein has been reassessed.

Therefore, the actual loss of income for three months would to Rs.18,972/- (i.e.,
Rs.6,324/- X 3 months).

The said rate of interest is maintained; accordingly, the original claimant herein shall be entitled to 7.5% of interest per annum on the additional amount of compensation from the date of filing of the Claim Petition till its realization.

18. Thus, in view of the above discussion, the impugned judgment and award stands modified to the aforesaid extent and the captioned appeal preferred by the original claimant/appellant herein stands partly allowed.
19. Respondent No.3 - Insurance Company shall deposit the enhanced amount of compensation along with interest within a period of six weeks from today.
Upon depositing the said amount, the learned Tribunal shall disburse the entire awarded amount to the original claimant/appellant herein (deducting deficit Court fee, if any), after due verification.
20. Statutory amount, if any, lying deposited with the Registry of this Court shall be transmitted to the learned Tribunal concerned forthwith.
No order as to costs.
21. Pending application, if any, stands disposed of, accordingly.
